ECE 6390 / Antennas and arrays

Gain and matching

From the figure to the physics

Fig. 1 shows how directivity, radiation efficiency and mismatch use different power references.

Radiation intensity U(θ, φ) is in W/sr. Total radiated power is Pᵣₐd = ∫₀²π∫₀π U sin θ dθ dφ. Directivity is D = 4πU/Pᵣₐd; a forward-only model sets backward intensity to zero while retaining this definition.

For any peak-normalized power shape p, D(θ, φ) = 4πp/∫p dΩ. Integration angles are radians, with solid-angle measure sin θ dθ dφ; uniformly spaced angle samples are not equal-area samples. Squared field magnitude supplies intensity shape before this normalization.

Radiation efficiency ηᵣ relates radiated power to accepted power, so G = ηᵣD. With a real reference impedance, reflected power fraction is |Γ|² and realized gain is (1 − |Γ|²)ηᵣD. Polarization coupling is another factor applied at its appropriate link reference.

Example

With 100 W incident, |Γ|² = 0.10, and ηᵣ = 0.75, accepted power is 90 W and radiated power is 67.5 W. For D = 8, gain is 6 and realized gain is 5.4, both linear.

    Practice

    1. A plotted pattern peaks at 1. What additional information is needed to turn it into absolute gain?

    Separate angular normalization from conversion between incident, accepted, and radiated power.

    Integrate the power pattern over the full radiating solid angle to obtain directivity, then apply radiation efficiency and the required mismatch reference. A unit relative peak alone supplies none of those absolute gain values.
